Representative comments P2
(Expert comments [D] / Observation logs [OL] / pilot comments [GPI])

column1: 1: SL Video Quality and Content Accuracy

column3: (D1) “Each step should be clearly demonstrated visually; however, the clip jumps directly to the fragment, limiting the visibility of intermediate steps.”
(D2) “If the video size is reduced and displayed alongside images and text, it may be easier to understand.”
(D3) “Adjust the caption to a single line and recheck spelling.”
(D4) “Reduce the video size so it can be displayed together with images and text.”
(D5) “The SL for ‘rice menu’ and ‘som tam’ is still incorrect.”
(OL1) “The video is not responsive and lacks a close button, causing usability issues across different mobile devices.”

column2: 2.1 Menu Structure Clarity and Logical Consistency
column3: (D6) “Users may be confused about whether they are required to select certain sub-items; for example, whether squid must be selected for Yentafo, even though squid is already an inherent component of the dish.”
(D7) “General made-to-order menu items should be reviewed and expanded to provide more comprehensive coverage.”
(D8) “When the mobile phone is held in landscape orientation, users may not be able to see the overall interface.”
(D9) “Using the phone in landscape orientation prevents users from viewing the complete menu overview.”
(OL2) “Scrolling through ingredients requires excessive vertical scrolling, which makes the interaction feel inconvenient.”
(D10) “Users do not realize that they need to tap on images in the food categories to view details.”

(D11) “The main menu page should clearly indicate that food category images are tappable, as users are unaware that more details are available. Thumbnails or symbols should be added to indicate that images can be tapped to access specific menu items.”
(D12) “Overall, the interface is easy to understand, but users may not know which menus are tappable or whether there are no further options.”
(D13) “It is suggested to modify the button icon to display a handshape representing sign language with all five fingers, instead of only two fingers.”
(D14) “Additional iconography could be added to make the interface easier to understand for everyone.”

(GPI1) “The menu page should include additional menu options; for example, allowing users to order multiple made-to-order dishes (e.g. pork fried rice and vegetable fried rice) from the same restaurant, rather than being limited to only two sets.”
(D15) “The summarized spoken message should use a real human voice, as it would be easier to understand.”
(OL3) “On the order summary page, users are unsure whether the audio has already been played and worry that hearing vendors may not have heard it.”
(GPI2) “On the summary page, a status indicator should be added to show whether the spoken audio has finished playing.”
(OL4) “Hearing researchers observed that the audio output was interrupted and had inconsistent tone, as evidenced by confused facial expressions and difficulty understanding among hearing vendors.”

column2: 4.4 Cognitive Load Reduction for Deaf Users
column3: (D16) “On the audio summary page, only the spoken audio should be presented; text such as ‘playing audio’ should be removed, as Deaf users tend to read all on-screen text, which may cause confusion.”
